stated: The Conservative Party will expand mental health support by extending Mental Health Support Teams to 100% of schools and colleges by 2030, opening early support hubs for ages 11-25 in every community by 2030, increasing NHS Talking Therapies by 50%, and boosting Individual Placement and Support capacity by 140,000 places.

source.quote: Expand coverage of Mental Health Support Teams from 50% to 100% of schools and colleges in England by 2030. Open early support hubs for those aged 11-25 in every local community by 2030. Increase the planned expansion of NHS Talking Therapies by 50%... Boost the capacity of Individual Placement and Support for Severe Mental Illness by 140,000 places.

bearing_set.reason: Expanding NHS Talking Therapies by 50% and rolling out Mental Health Support Teams directly increases mental health access — an explicit O3 indicator — affecting waiting times and treatment capacity.

Mental Health Support Teams in 100% of schools/colleges and early support hubs for ages 11–25 directly target educational settings and are materially linked to attainment, especially for disadvantaged pupils.

Individual Placement and Support (IPS) is a clinically-backed employment programme for people with mental health conditions; adding 140,000 places directly affects employment rates and job retention for this group.

Large-scale unfunded-as-stated spending across four separate programmes (school teams, community hubs, NHS Talking Therapies uplift, IPS expansion) would widen the fiscal gap if not offset — the mechanism is direct public expenditure with no stated revenue source, moving the 'is spending funded vs borrowed' indicator.

membership_note: Four genuine bearings: the core healthcare access effect (O3), the education-setting mental health infrastructure (O7), the employment-support arm (O4), and the public finances cost of a substantial multi-programme spending pledge without a stated funding mechanism (O12).
